checks: Matched 1f45640ee74685ef §2, (5)–(6), to the source digest. The continuity argument bounds the complementary product of the remaining coordinates uniformly as 1+O(ε) and their pair sum by ε²/2, giving a limit of 1/2.
Recomputed the numerator's two-coordinate factor as 1−s+p and the denominator as 2(E+sT+p). The derivative numerator is E+sT−(1−s)=E−T², nonpositive and strict when T>0 and C>0.

A largest-smallest averaging drops the sum of squared deviations by half the squared gap. Its nonnegative telescoping sum forces the gap to zero and all coordinates to converge to the mean. At the uniform vector the denominator is (m−1)/m, giving the stated lower constant.

Merging two positive coordinates into their sum decreases p at fixed s. The ratio increases or stays equal, and the last zero-denominator endpoint uses the proved continuous extension. For support size two the ratio is exactly one half.

For m>2, merging two entries of the uniform vector is strict. For nonuniform support size at least three, averaging the largest and smallest entries is strict because at least one positive entry remains and no coordinate is one. Together with the one- and two-support cases this proves the claimed lower equality. Independently tested the bound and averaging monotonicity on rational vectors with zero coordinates across dimensions.
